newsitem.title: USA: Ford sets new head of Brazil, Argentina unit.
newsitem.headline: Ford sets new head of Brazil, Argentina unit.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Tuesday it named James Padilla a vice president and appointed him president of Ford Brazil and Argentina, effective November 1.
Padilla, 50 years old, replaces Gurminder Bedi, who returns to the United States for a new assignment that has not been announced yet, a Ford spokesman said.

Padilla is currently vehicle line director for performance luxury of Vehicle Center 3, a Dearborn-based unit that develops rear-wheel drive cars. He will be located in Sao Paulo, Brazil, and will report to Ed Hagenlocker, president of Ford Automotive Operations.

Padilla, who holds degrees in chemical engineering and economics, joined the U.S. No. 2 automaker in 1966 and has held manufacturing positions with the Escort/Tracer, Contour/Mystique and Taurus/Sable car programs.
Padilla was also director of the small car segment within Car Product Development, and director of engineering and manufacturing for Ford's luxury Jaguar program.
